record.paper_title: Everything You Always Wanted to Know About How Causal Set Theory Can Help with Open Questions in Cosmology, but Were Afraid to Ask
record.original_question: What cosmological observations could distinguish causal-set or other quantum-gravity effects from alternative explanations, given that a quantum theory may suggest or predict an effect without being unique in doing so and that contrived classical explanations may mimic the same observations?

evidence.quote: Cosmology offers a rich testing ground for approaches to quantum gravity.
There is no smoking gun evidence yet for any particular quantum gravity effect in cosmological observations.

Part of the challenge is that while a quantum theory may suggest an explanation for or even predict an effect, it is not unique in doing so; sometimes, one cannot even rule out a contrived classical explanation for the very same effects.

artifact.category_tag: causal set theory and quantum gravity phenomenology
artifact.self_contained_problem:
In causal set theory, spacetime is modeled as a locally finite partially ordered set (C, ≺), where elements represent spacetime events, the partial order ≺ encodes causal precedence, and local finiteness requires every order interval {z : x ≺ z ≺ y} to be finite. A continuum spacetime (M, g) is said to be approximated by a causal set if (C, ≺) arises (up to a fluctuation scale) as a Poisson sprinkling of points into (M, g) with the induced causal order. Cosmological observables (e.g. the cosmic microwave background power spectrum and non-Gaussianities, the late-time accelerated expansion attributed to a dark-energy density Λ, large-scale structure statistics, polarization birefringence, the primordial gravitational-wave spectrum, and discrete Lorentz-invariant diffusion of massive and massless particles) can in principle carry imprints of an underlying discrete causal structure.

Identify a concrete set of cosmological observations O = {O_1, O_2, …} and quantitative predictions P_CS(O_i) derivable from causal set theory (or, more generally, from a candidate quantum theory of gravity) such that:

(a) For each O_i there exists a derivation of P_CS(O_i) from the causal-set framework (for example, the everpresent-Λ prediction ⟨Λ⟩ ∼ 1/√V with characteristic fluctuations, or specific deviations in particle propagators induced by sprinkling-based d'Alembertians).

(b) No classical (non-quantum-gravity) cosmological model — including inflationary models with tuned potentials, modified-gravity theories, and otherwise unconstrained matter sectors — can reproduce P_CS(O_i) for all i simultaneously without invoking parameter choices that are demonstrably fine-tuned or otherwise pathological by a precisely formulated criterion (to be specified, e.g. Bayesian evidence ratios, information-theoretic naturalness measures, or genericity within the relevant theory space).

(c) The combined signature {P_CS(O_i)}_i is, under criterion (b), distinguishable from the predictions of competing quantum-gravity frameworks (such as loop quantum cosmology, string-theoretic cosmologies, or asymptotically safe gravity).

Equivalently: construct an observational discriminator — a measurable functional D on cosmological data — together with a proof that D attains values in a region R_CS predicted by causal set theory but excluded (modulo the fine-tuning criterion of (b)) from the predictions of all classical and competing quantum-gravity alternatives.
artifact.status_search_result: No "smoking gun" cosmological observation uniquely attributable to causal set theory or any other quantum-gravity proposal has been identified. The everpresent-Λ prediction of causal sets remains a leading candidate distinguishing signature but is not yet experimentally confirmed nor demonstrably unique to causal sets, and current reviews continue to list the problem of observational discrimination as open.

status_evidence.title: Causal Set Theory (Living Reviews in Relativity, Surya 2019)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses phenomenology of causal sets, including the everpresent-Λ proposal and swerves, noting that observational signatures remain to be conclusively established.
status_evidence.claim: Distinguishing causal-set signatures from alternatives is an active open research direction.

status_evidence.title: Everpresent Λ (Ahmed, Dodelson, Greene, Sorkin)
status_evidence.snippet: Predicts a fluctuating cosmological constant of order 1/sqrt(V) motivated by causal set quantum gravity.
status_evidence.claim: A specific causal-set prediction exists but has not been uniquely confirmed by data.
